subject: Transient slab allocation proposal — Helios AI renewal
messages:
From: Akash Reddy <akash@helios.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@helios.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 renewal — short-term GPU bump request

Marcus —

We just finished a post-mortem on last week's inference spike; the platform team is asking for a short-term runway to avoid throttling while we finalize our model parallelism changes. Current committed Dedicated fleet is fine for baseline, but we saw sustained 220% of expected concurrency for ~3 hours on Sep 16 and again last night.

Can Redwood offer a transient allocation (2–3 weeks) of additional GPU slots or a burst tranche we can pull from? We would like the ability to convert that into committed capacity at renewal if usage stabilizes.

I attached the utilization snapshot and a short sample of latency outliers. What information do you need from us to size the bump?

Thanks,
Akash
Platform Lead, Helios AI
Helios AI

Attachments: helios_utilization_snapshot_202709_Q3.csv, gpu-runner-latency-sample.png
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Akash Reddy <akash@helios.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal — short-term GPU bump request

Hi Akash —

Appreciate the data and the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provision a transient slab (2–4 week window) that sits behind your Dedicated pool and can be converted to committed capacity at renewal with a pro-rated credit.

High-level proposal attached (transient-slab-proposal-v1.xlsx). Key points:
- Recommend a 48-slot NV72 slab to cover the 2.2x concurrency at P95 workloads for 3–4 hours/day, based on your September profile.
- Default routing: traffic will spill to the transient slab only when Dedicated pool saturation exceeds 85% for >5 minutes to avoid unnecessary usage.
- Conversion path: any portion converted to committed at renewal will apply usage credits for the remaining transient period.
- Cost impact: transient is billed at a blended burst rate; converting locks in a discounted commit rate.

Next steps I suggest: (1) Ben and Kim run a quick capacity simulation against the CSV to validate the 48-slot suggestion, (2) we finalize SLA for burst routing, and (3) legal gets a short amendment drafted for pro-rata conversion.

CCing Ben and Kim to validate sizing and operational constraints.

— Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: transient-slab-proposal-v1.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal — short-term GPU bump request

Quick sanity check after running the CSV through the queueing simulator:
- 48 NV72 slots looks conservative but safe. At observed peak shapes, 36 slots would cover 95% of spikes but leave a tail risk for multi-hour events.
- If Helios is willing to accept a 250ms P95 degradation during the first hour of spill, we could reduce to 40 slots to save ~12% on transient billing.
- We need to confirm whether their workload can accept preemption of background batch jobs. Our slab routing currently respects batch priority tags, but we should confirm Helios' job labels.

Operational actions for Kimberly: can we carve a 40-slot transient slab and set the spill threshold at 85% with a 5-minute debounce? That would be a cheaper option to propose and still protect them from throttles.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Akash Reddy <akash@helios.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal — short-term GPU bump request

Hi all —

I ran the topology and routing constraints through the orchestration planner. Notes:
- We can provision a 40-slot transient NV72 slab in us-west-2 with the spill threshold Ben suggested (85% sustained for 5 minutes).
- Routing will preserve your priority tagging: inference:online calls will spill first, batch jobs will be preemptible unless you opt otherwise.
- Observability: we will add a per-route metric feed and a cost ledger for the transient slab so Helios can see tokens/slots consumed in near real-time.
- SLA: transient slab will have best-effort latency targets; we can add an optional premium for guaranteed latency during spill windows (adds ~18% to transient rate).

Akash — if you confirm: (1) 40 slots, (2) preserve online priority and preempt batches, (3) 3-week default duration with one-time extension option — we'll prepare the amendment and enable the slab by next Tuesday (Oct 5).

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: none (operational plan will be added to Drive link once signed)
From: Akash Reddy <akash@helios.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal — short-term GPU bump request

Thanks Marcus, Ben, Kim — this looks good. We confirm the following:
- Accept the 40-slot transient NV72 slab in us-west-2
- Preserve online priority; batch jobs are preemptible
- Default duration 3 weeks starting Oct 5, with one 2-week extension option
- We will review conversion at renewal — please add the pro-rata credit language to the amendment.

I'll have procurement issue a PO after we receive the amendment. Please send the amendment + Drive link for observability docs and I'll route for signatures.

Akash
Platform Lead, Helios AI
akash@helios.ai
